build: Triangle disk release from the C64Games archive

comments.text: Actor type three. Initialize walking direction toward the player, animation dividers, health one and fall state. Test player overlap and projectile-character damage, animate four facing-dependent walk shapes, turn at blocking terrain and fall according to the vertical tables. The descending-player contact path changes the actor to its flattened state and can bounce the player; its second coordinate comparison uses player X. Wheel/immunity contact or the screen flash releases it through an explosion and awards 100 points.

Operand byte 1 of the BPL instruction at $6C02, within this level's existing actor or display routine. It is not an independent instruction entry. The shared call to $6C03 selects music only in overlays that contain the music driver; this level has an actor branch operand here.

Continuation of the type-three initialization at $6C00: store its animation divider, derive phase and health values by shifts, clear its behavior state and choose facing. A music call to this address belongs to flight overlays, whose bytes are different.

Actor type four. When its screen position is in the permitted region, convert the actor into one of seven character-effect records: character column, row, random start delay and alternating phase. Release the actor after allocation, or when the records are full. Actors outside the allocation region wait unless they have left the outer viewport bounds.

Walk seven active character-effect records and retain an any-active flag at $0800. After each record's initial delay and animation divider, require an empty destination cell, draw the selected two-character $BC/$BD or $BE/$BF pair in both screen buffers, colour it five and move its row upward. Bounds or a nonempty cell remove the record.

Actor type five. The main state chooses an entry side, follows a signed vertical arc while moving horizontally, changes its facing-dependent sprite with the arc phase and drops further type-five actors. Dropped actors animate three shapes, descend two pixels per update and explode on solid terrain. Contact, a projectile or screen flash can destroy either state for 200 points.

Actor type six. Initialize a hidden wait state, health ten and an emergence animation. When the pose reaches a facing-specific firing frame and the player is within its horizontal test, enter the active firing state. Its divider allocates horizontal type-sixteen projectiles, and its pose alternates around shots. Player/projectile damage checks are skipped while the hidden state is zero; destruction awards 300 points.

Actor type seven. Subtype zero is a hidden emitter that allocates falling state-one actors near the top of the playfield. A falling actor reacts differently to ordinary solid terrain, glyph $A5 and the $18/$C4-$C7 effect glyphs: it can enter a short terminal animation or a walking state. Walkers turn at terrain, animate and can allocate a jittering state-three actor. State three changes position with CIA-timer XORs and decrements the unindexed counter $BC23. Other accepted destruction paths award 150 points.

Actor type eight. Allocate three extra slots and arrange a four-sprite body, aborting if allocation cannot finish. The leader has health 64, chooses horizontal movement toward the player and tests terrain before shifting all four X positions together. Its projectile scan covers multiple character rows. Destruction awards 1000 points and changes all components into individually moving fragments, which can hurt the player before their terminal animation.
Four half-pixel X offsets for the component slots of actor type eight.
Four pixel-Y offsets paired with the component X positions at $769F.
Four initial component states: one leader and three followers, assigned through the allocated slot directory.
Four initial sprite numbers for the composite enemy; animation toggles each through XOR four.
Two facing-selected horizontal increments for the composite leader.
Four signed horizontal steps used after the composite separates into moving fragments.

Actor type nine. Subtype zero periodically allocates state-one actors at its position with random horizontal direction and movement divider. State-one actors follow the shared vertical curve at $79AC, bounce from terrain and turn at horizontal obstructions. Any accepted projectile/protected-contact/screen-flash destruction awards 100 points.

Actor type ten. The initial state supplies a solid platform and changes to its reward state when struck by a projectile. Repeated qualified hits count down its reward counter, create bouncing collectible slots with randomized subtypes, and finally award 5000 points before explosion. Separate overlap paths let the player stand on it or bump it from below, maintaining the shared platform-contact flags. Spawned reward actors move with a signed trajectory until they become ordinary type-two pickups.
Nine signed vertical offsets for the platform's bump response, selected by its descending response counter.
Thirty signed vertical offsets for newly launched rewards before they settle into the ordinary collectible behavior.

Actor type twelve. Alternate its shape on a two-call divider, enable multicolour, follow player X and form Y from player posture and wheel offsets. During the ascending part of a jump increment player Y. The picture's identity remains to be named from the graphics.

Actor type eleven. Animate its sprite on a two-call divider, enable multicolour, set colour one and follow the player's X/Y with one of three vertical offsets. This copy adds CLC before forming Y, and uses a fixed colour instead of the level-1-1 background test.

Actor type thirteen. Initialize a random-position explosion, choose a SID effect voice through $7AD8, and honor its slot's start delay at $AF88. While the shared pending count is nonzero, allocate another type-thirteen actor and consume one count. An eligible grounded player at Y at least $80 can start the automatic rightward exit through the walking hook. Animate seven explosion shapes and release the slot afterward.
Four SID voice-state offsets, zero/seven/fourteen/seven, selected by the low two CIA-timer bits when an exit explosion starts.
Set terrain properties for glyphs $C1/$C2 to $D3, their colours to one, and the property of glyph $80 to zero, then enter the per-update callback.

Adjust player Y at the automated-exit X coordinate, clear effect/control flags, update the seven rising character effects and select local background/effect behavior from camera-coordinate regions. One region patches a series of source-map cells. Other regions invoke the water/splash updater or the collapsing-strip updater.
Replace the listed source-map cells with supplied encoded block values when the callback reaches its selected camera region. The stores include the sequence of cells at $A74C through $AF1E.

Test player-adjacent terrain for the $C4-$C7 effect range and manage the type-twelve attached splash. Rotate the character strip at $C61D-$C63F and generate the ripple rows through masks $AF5B. Select player colours from the supporting tile and manage the type-eleven surface splash, then advance the three-frame glyph-$A4 animation.
Operand byte 1 of the LDX instruction at $7C0B, within the existing level actor or raster code. It is not another routine entry.
Operand byte 1 of the LDX instruction at $7CC2, within the existing level actor or raster code. It is not another routine entry.

Raise four local control/effect flags. During player death restore the initial camera, map pointers and checkpoint position. Walk six strips and activate a pending strip when its world X is near the camera. Shift four rows downward in both screen buffers and colour RAM and blank the exposed top. When its step counter reaches twenty-one, clear the corresponding source-map cells in rows four and five and deactivate it. The loaded counters start at sixteen.

Actor type fourteen. Wait for a grounded player and centred fine scrolling, then install the special display/camera hooks and clear smaller actors. Draw a four-column, two-band overhead body, move it horizontally with a reversing CIA-selected step, and drop a sprite attack that can split into four arcing fragments. Scan nine terrain-character spans for shots and subtract shared damage from initial health $01BC. Destruction restores normal hooks, awards 10000 points and replaces the slots with four life collectibles and seven explosions.

Convert the body's half-pixel X to four hardware sprite X positions and high bits, place sprites three through six at Y $38, assign their first-band shapes and hit-flash colour, and set the next band marker.
Move the four body sprites to Y $4D, update the falling attack's ninth-X-bit position on sprite seven, and schedule the next raster stage through $81CC.
After its alignment delay select four second-band shapes $B2-$B5 and schedule the attack-fragment stage.
Operand byte 2 of the STY instruction at $8154, within the existing level actor or raster code. It is not another routine entry.
Operand byte 2 of the STY instruction at $8158, within the existing level actor or raster code. It is not another routine entry.
Operand byte 2 of the STY instruction at $815C, within the existing level actor or raster code. It is not another routine entry.
Operand byte 2 of the STY instruction at $8160, within the existing level actor or raster code. It is not another routine entry.

If the four-fragment attack is active, advance its vertical curve and four signed horizontal positions, then draw the fragments on sprites three through six. End the attack when its Y crosses the stored player-height boundary and schedule the final cleanup stage.
Operand byte 1 of the LDY instruction at $81CA, within the existing level actor or raster code. It is not another routine entry.
Install the supplied next handler A/X and raster compare Y, then return through the shared register-restoring IRQ exit.
Hide the falling attack sprite's X and high bit, restore the status-panel handler from the saved pointer at $071B/$071C, and schedule raster line $D5.
Four AND masks for replacing the X high bits of hardware sprites three through six in the overhead enemy display.
Four high-bit setting masks paired with $81EF.
Four signed horizontal steps for the fragments emitted by the overhead enemy's falling attack.
Nine character offsets selecting the silhouette spans scanned for character-shot hits.
Nine span lengths paired with the offsets at $81FB; most are two cells and the last is twelve.
Eleven replacement actor types for destruction: four collectibles and seven explosions.
Eleven subtype bytes paired with $820D. The four collectible entries are initialized life rewards; the other seven initialize explosions.

Actor type fifteen. Wait for a grounded player, centred scrolling and the camera threshold, then install a three-column by seven-band sprite display and disable the ordinary camera. Emerge from the right, update terrain-based beam effects and two sprite projectiles, and accept shot damage at two selected terrain cells after emergence. Its health word at $8A06 starts at 300. Death restores the normal hooks, sets a pending count of fifty exit explosions and awards 15000 points.

On the emergence divider move the three body X coordinates left until the first reaches seven. Update the supporting terrain pointer and glyph-$C0 fill mask from the pixel phase. At a selected phase draw the sloped terrain edge from the eighteen offsets at $8A10; when emergence finishes, clear its flag and silence the effect voice.

Form terrain and colour pointers relative to the boss anchor. Cycle one body colour and a fifteen-step colour fade during the attack countdown. At selected phases draw or erase long character strips using $9E/$9F and $C1/$C2, and animate mirrored glyph pairs from $8A66 into $C4F0 and $C608/$C610. These terrain characters participate in the properties set by level initialization.

Outside emergence, decrement the attack countdown and at two phase values choose one three-entry half of nine six-entry arrays at $9DAC-$9DE1. Copy those values into the live shape and bitmap-address matrices in $F7C5-$F7FF, reshape seven terrain rows using the width arrays at $8A22/$8A29, and request the paired sprite-projectile launch when both launch records are idle. A live read watchpoint confirmed the copy of $9DD1 to $F7F0.

Walk two projectile records on sprites six and seven. A negative launch request installs a per-projectile delay, initial position, high-X mask and vertical curve. After the delay, follow the 23-entry vertical curve, move X left by four pixels, animate four shapes, and deactivate after crossing the side boundary.
Replace the two projectile X high bits and write their X/Y registers using the masks and offsets at $8A9F-$8AA4.

Test active projectiles and the full seven-band body against the player through the shared rectangle helper. Convert projectile nine-bit X to half pixels and suppress player damage in wheel/invulnerability state.

Compare player coordinates with the supplied rectangle in $DD-$E0. On accepted overlap call the resident player-damage hook unless wheel mode or invulnerability is active. Both large-enemy controllers in this level call this helper.

After emergence inspect two adjacent terrain cells at the weak-point offset. Consume a character at or above $C8 with $FF and subtract its shared damage from the health word at $8A06/$8A07. A hit clears all twenty-one body colours; health underflow sets the death countdown and advances the actor state.

Alternate body colours and request the death effect while the countdown runs, then erase the associated terrain strip, restore ordinary camera/multiplexer hooks and clear sprite priority. Initialize an exit-explosion actor in slot ten and pending count fifty, request the palette flash and temporary blocking state, and award 15000 points.
Draw both sprite projectiles, clear band cursors and place the first body's three sprite Y values from $F790. Set the next-row marker immediately before that Y.

Write the first three body shape pointers to both screen directories. Choose the first column X according to emergence and fine scroll, form the other columns at twenty-four-pixel intervals, and install the shared ninth-X bits and three row colours.

Multiplex sprites three through five over the seven body bands using the live shape, colour and Y matrices. At a sensitive fine-scroll alignment exchange the next bitmap row through $88F8 and restore it through $8962. Finish by reinstalling the status-panel IRQ pointer.

Remove actor types below fourteen, install the return stub as the camera hook and clear the pending screen-copy continuations to the common IRQ exit. Both large-enemy initializers use this display setup.
Convert the last body band's Y minus $25 to a screen row pointer, retain it in $BCA8/$BCA9 and derive a character column from the first body X. Beam drawing and damage tests use this anchor.
Convert A plus the separately supplied ninth-X selector in Y to an eight-bit half-pixel coordinate by setting carry and rotating A right.
Mutable little-endian health word loaded as $012C, decimal 300. The weak-point routine subtracts character damage and begins destruction on underflow.
High byte of the two-byte boss health counter at $8A06, initially $01 with low byte $2C, for 300 total damage units.
Eight masks indexed by the first body X coordinate's low three bits, copied to all eight rows of glyph $C0 as the boss emerges.
Eighteen offsets defining the sloped terrain edge during emergence. The mutable horizontal origin at $8A30 is added before drawing its row.
Seven width/edge values selected for the first pose phase, one per terrain row reshaped by $8512.
Seven alternate width/edge values for the other pose phase.
Mutable character-column origin for the terrain edge, decremented during emergence and added to its row offsets.
Thirty-six colours selected by a descending wrapping cursor and written into one body-matrix entry during the beam sequence.
Fifteen colour values indexed by the beam fade cursor. The updater grows or shrinks the cursor and writes the selected colour across its terrain strip.
Two end offsets selecting the two sixteen-byte glyph-pair animation frames beginning at $8A66.
Two sixteen-byte glyph-pair frames. The updater copies one to $C4F0-$C4FF and reverses its two eight-byte halves into $C608/$C610.
Twenty-three retained signed step bytes. A launch starts at index twenty-two and reads down through one; zero takes the constant-Y phase instead of reading entry zero.
Two initial delays, zero and fifty update calls, for the paired sprite projectiles.
Two offsets, zero and two, selecting the X/Y register pairs of hardware sprites six and seven.
Two ninth-X-bit masks for the paired projectile sprites.
AND masks paired with $8AA1 for replacing the projectile high bits.
Two retained zero bytes between the projectile-mask tables and the actor-record streams at $8AA7. No additional projectile entry is inferred from them.
